## Summary

Under Section 7(1) of the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008, an LLP must have **at least two designated partners**.

Both must be individuals, and **at least one must be resident in India**. Where partners are body corporates, at least two individuals who are partners or nominees of those body corporates must act as designated partners.

Legal currentness is unverified. This is legal information, not legal advice.

## Relevant quotation

> “Every limited liability partnership shall have at least two designated partners who are individuals and at least one of them shall be a resident in India.”

## Summary

Under the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 (FEMA), a **current account transaction** means a transaction **other than a capital account transaction**.

It includes, among other things:

- Payments connected with foreign trade, ordinary business, services, and short-term banking or credit facilities.
- Interest payments on loans and net income from investments.
- Remittances for the living expenses of parents, spouse, and children residing abroad.
- Expenses relating to foreign travel, education, and medical care of parents, spouse, and children.

Under section 5, a person may sell or draw foreign exchange through an authorised person when the transaction is a current account transaction. However, the Central Government may impose reasonable restrictions in the public interest, in consultation with the Reserve Bank.

The Foreign Exchange Management (Current Account Transactions) Rules, 2000 provide that certain current account transactions may be prohibited or may require prior approval, depending on the applicable schedule.

## Relevant quotation

> “current account transaction” means a transaction other than a capital account transaction and without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing such transaction includes, —  
> (i) payments due in connection with foreign trade, other current business, services, and short-term banking and credit facilities in the ordinary course of business,  
> (ii) payments due as interest on loans and as net income from investments,  
> (iii) remittances for living expenses of parents, spouse and children residing abroad, and  
> (iv) expenses in connection with foreign travel, education and medical care of parents, spouse and children.

Legal currentness is unverified. This is legal information, not legal advice.

## Summary

Under section 2(v) of the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 (FEMA), a **“person resident in India”** includes:

- **An individual** residing in India for more than **182 days during the preceding financial year**, subject to the exclusions and exceptions below.
- **Any person or body corporate** registered or incorporated in India.
- An **office, branch or agency in India** owned or controlled by a person resident outside India.
- An **office, branch or agency outside India** owned or controlled by a person resident in India.

For an individual, the 182-day test is not conclusive by itself:

- A person who has left India, or stays outside India, for employment, business or vocation outside India, or for another purpose indicating an intention to stay outside India for an uncertain period, is excluded.
- A person who has come to or stays in India is excluded if the purpose is not employment, business or vocation in India, or another purpose indicating an intention to stay in India for an uncertain period.

A person who is not resident in India is treated as a **“person resident outside India.”**

## Relevant quotation

> “a person residing in India for more than one hundred and eighty-two days during the course of the preceding financial year”  
> subject to the exclusions relating to the person’s purpose and intention of staying in or outside India.

This answer is based on the supplied FEMA text. Legal currentness has not been independently verified, and this is legal information, not legal advice.

## Summary

Under section 2(v) of the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999, a **“person resident in India”** means:

1. **An individual** who has resided in India for more than **182 days during the preceding financial year**, subject to these exclusions:

     - to take up employment outside India;
     - to carry on a business or vocation outside India; or
     - for another purpose indicating an intention to stay outside India for an uncertain period.
   - A person who has come to or stays in India otherwise than:
     - to take up employment in India;
     - to carry on a business or vocation in India; or
     - for another purpose indicating an intention to stay in India for an uncertain period.

2. **Any person or body corporate registered or incorporated in India.**

3. **An office, branch or agency in India** owned or controlled by a person resident outside India.

4. **An office, branch or agency outside India** owned or controlled by a person resident in India.

A person who does not fall within this definition is treated as a **“person resident outside India.”**

- Any person or body corporate registered or incorporated in India.
- An office, branch or agency in India owned or controlled by a person resident outside India.
- An office, branch or agency outside India owned or controlled by a person resident in India.

A person who does not qualify as resident in India is treated as a **“person resident outside India.”**

> “ ‘person resident in India’ means —  
> (i) a person residing in India for more than one hundred and eighty-two days during the course of the preceding financial year”  

The definition is subject to the employment, business, vocation and intention-based exclusions stated in section 2(v)(i)(A) and (B).
